The appointment went on longer than necessary.  I felt I knew what would help given my limited options.  I'm extremely  resilient despite everything.  I've coped with my struggles for 50+ years yet she didn't seem to appreciate that.  Could have got the appointment completed in under 5 minutes but she proceeded to press me on my reasons for wanting my Summary Care Record.  She did not respect my boundaries when I told her my reason for requiring my Summary Care Record wasn't any of her business, just her way of asserting control and gathering information.  Yet, she still pressed me multiple times for further details, not respecting patient  boundaries.  This further antagonised me and  given that the reason I required the Summary Care Record was due to multiple dismissals for a diagnosis now privately acquired it didn't go down well.   She's dismissed me in the past when I was perimenopausal, progesterone intolerant which I didn't realise at the time, and undiagnosed ADHD.  I was refused any hrt input at the appointment, she dismissed my concerns as being down to "anxiety  not hormones".  🤔🙄. Give me strength.  I was early 50s with no hrt, progesterone intolerant  and undiagnosed ADHD.  The issue was most certainly hormones as I later discovered I was progesterone intolerant.

Five stars for the ability to antagonise the patient so badly it impacts their mental After a serious accident recently (being critical, 7 spinal fractures, most of my left hand side rib cage broken, then bleeding on the lung thereafter) my address was updated by the hospital. The new address is a 2minute walk from my birth address and I have been told I need to move surgery.
I emailed a kindly worded email, suggesting this may not be the most practical time to switch doctors, but given the reply from the surgery manager, it seems the postcode rule is more important than a patient working through trauma.
